syllabus_version.title: CBSE Curriculum for the Academic Year 2026-27

topics.title: Human geography: dualism and definitions
topics.ncert_sections: Introduction; Human Geography Defined

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why the dichotomy between physical and human geography is not a valid one and why nature and humans must be seen holistically.
Identify the definitions of human geography given by Ratzel, Ellen C. Semple and Paul Vidal de la Blache and their key ideas.

topics.title: Nature of human geography and naturalisation of humans
topics.ncert_sections: Nature of Human Geography; The Naturalisation of Humans

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish elements of the physical environment from elements of material culture created by human beings.
Explain how understanding of natural laws leads to technology and how technology reflects cultural development.
Describe environmental determinism and the naturalisation of humans in primitive societies.

topics.title: Humanisation of nature: possibilism and neo-determinism
topics.ncert_sections: Humanisation of Nature; Neodeterminism

concepts.learning_objective: Explain possibilism as the creation of possibilities by humans using technology and resources of the environment.
Identify imprints of human activity that form the cultural landscape.
Explain Griffith Taylor's neo-determinism (stop and go determinism) as a middle path between determinism and possibilism.

topics.title: Broad stages and thrust of human geography
topics.ncert_sections: Table 1.1

concepts.learning_objective: Sequence the broad stages of human geography and state the approach of each period.
Describe the spatial organisation phase and the quantitative revolution.
Explain how post-modernism questioned grand generalisations and stressed local context.

topics.title: Schools of thought, fields and sub-fields of human geography
topics.ncert_sections: Box on schools of thought; Fields and Sub-fields of Human Geography; Table 1.2

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish the welfare (humanistic), radical and behavioural schools of thought that emerged in the 1970s.
Match fields and sub-fields of human geography with their sister disciplines in the social sciences.

chapters.title: The World Population: Distribution, Density and Growth

topics.title: Patterns of population distribution and density
topics.ncert_sections: Patterns of Population Distribution in the World; Density of Population

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the uneven distribution of the world's population across its land area.
Calculate and interpret the density of population as persons per sq km.

topics.title: Factors influencing the distribution of population
topics.ncert_sections: Factors Influencing the Distribution of Population

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how water, landforms, climate and soils affect where people live.
Explain how minerals, urbanisation and industrialisation concentrate population.
Recognise how religious, cultural, political and government factors influence settlement.

topics.title: Population growth: basic concepts
topics.ncert_sections: Population Growth; Some Basic Concepts of Population Geography

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish growth of population in absolute numbers from the growth rate in per cent.
Compute natural growth and actual growth of population from births, deaths and migration.
Explain the conditions that produce positive or negative growth of population.

topics.title: Components of population change: births and deaths
topics.ncert_sections: Components of Population Change

concepts.learning_objective: Define and calculate the crude birth rate per thousand of population.
Define and calculate the crude death rate and relate falling mortality to population growth.

topics.title: Migration: origin, destination, push and pull factors
topics.ncert_sections: Migration

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish immigrants from emigrants and the place of origin from the place of destination.
Classify the push and pull factors that influence migration.

topics.title: Demographic transition
topics.ncert_sections: Demographic Transition

concepts.learning_objective: Describe fertility, mortality and population growth in the three stages of demographic transition.

topics.title: Population control measures
topics.ncert_sections: Population Control Measures

concepts.learning_objective: Identify family planning and other measures that help control population growth.
State Malthus's theory on population growth and food supply.

topics.title: Growth and development

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish growth as a quantitative, value-neutral change from development as a qualitative, value-positive change.
Explain why measuring development only by economic growth ignores changes in people's lives.

topics.title: The concept of human development

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the contributions of Mahbub-ul-Haq and Amartya Sen to the idea of human development.
Identify health, education and access to resources as the key areas of human development.
Explain how a lack of capability in health, education or resources limits people's choices.

topics.title: The four pillars of human development

concepts.learning_objective: Explain equity as equal access to opportunities irrespective of gender, race, income and caste.
Explain sustainability as continuity in the availability of opportunities across generations.
Explain productivity as human work efficiency and empowerment as the power to make choices.

topics.title: Approaches to human development
topics.ncert_sections: Table 3.1

concepts.learning_objective: Compare the income approach and the welfare approach to human development.
Compare the basic needs approach of the ILO with the capability approach of Amartya Sen.

topics.title: Measuring human development

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the indicators and weightage used in the human development index and interpret its scores.
Explain the human poverty index as a non-income measure of the shortfall in human development.
Describe Bhutan's Gross National Happiness as an alternative measure of progress.

topics.title: International comparisons
topics.ncert_sections: Tables 3.2, 3.3

concepts.learning_objective: Classify countries into very high, high, medium and low human development using HDI scores.
Explain why territorial size and per capita income are not directly related to human development.
Analyse how social-sector spending, political stability, freedom and equity shape human development levels.

topics.title: Economic activities and hunting and gathering

concepts.learning_objective: Explain what primary activities are and why they depend directly on the environment.
Describe the features, regions and commercialisation of hunting and gathering.

topics.title: Pastoralism: nomadic herding and commercial livestock rearing

concepts.learning_objective: Describe pastoral nomadism, its animals, regions and reasons for decline.
Explain transhumance with examples from the Himalayas and the tundra.
Explain the organised, scientific and capital-intensive nature of commercial livestock ranching.

topics.title: Subsistence agriculture: primitive and intensive

concepts.learning_objective: Describe slash and burn agriculture, its regional names and its problems.
Distinguish the two types of intensive subsistence agriculture of monsoon Asia.

topics.title: Plantation, extensive commercial grain and mixed farming

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the characteristics, crops and colonial origins of plantation agriculture.
Explain the features and regions of extensive commercial grain cultivation.
Describe the crops, livestock and practices of mixed farming.

topics.title: Dairy, Mediterranean agriculture, market gardening and factory farming

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the capital and labour needs, location and regions of commercial dairy farming.
Describe viticulture, citrus fruits and the winter advantage of Mediterranean agriculture.
Explain market gardening, truck farming and factory farming near urban markets.

topics.title: Farming organisation: co-operative and collective farming

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how co-operative farming works and where it has succeeded.
Describe the principle and working of collective farming (Kolkhoz) in the erstwhile Soviet Union.

topics.title: Mining: factors and methods

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the physical and economic factors that decide the profitability of mining.
Compare surface (open-cast) and underground (shaft) mining.

topics.title: Secondary activities and the meaning of manufacturing
topics.ncert_sections: Introduction; Manufacturing; 'Manufacturing' Industry and 'Manufacturing Industry'

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how secondary activities add value to natural resources by transforming raw materials into finished products.
Distinguish the literal meaning of manufacturing from its modern meaning and from the concept of an industry.

topics.title: Characteristics of modern large scale manufacturing
topics.ncert_sections: Characteristics of Modern Large Scale Manufacturing

concepts.learning_objective: Contrast the craft method with mass production of standardised parts.
Describe mechanisation, automation, technological innovation and the organisational needs of modern manufacturing.
Interpret why modern manufacturing is concentrated in a few small areas of the world.

topics.title: Factors of industrial location and footloose industries
topics.ncert_sections: Why do Large-scale Industries choose different locations?; Foot Loose Industries

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how access to markets and to raw materials influences where industries are located.
Explain the role of labour, energy, transport, government policy and agglomeration economies in industrial location.
Identify the features and the main locational factor of footloose industries.

topics.title: Classification of industries based on size
topics.ncert_sections: Classification of Manufacturing Industries; Industries based on Size

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the features of household or cottage manufacturing.
Distinguish small scale manufacturing from household industries and state its role in employment.
Describe large scale manufacturing and the two broad types of world industrial regions.

topics.title: Classification of industries based on inputs or raw materials
topics.ncert_sections: Industries based on Inputs/Raw Materials

concepts.learning_objective: Identify agro-based industries and explain the idea of agri-business.
Classify industries using ferrous, non-ferrous, non-metallic and chemical raw materials.
Identify raw materials that industries obtain from forests and animals.

topics.title: Classification of industries based on output and ownership
topics.ncert_sections: Industries Based On Output/Product; Industries Based on Ownership

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish basic industries from consumer goods industries using examples.
Differentiate public, private and joint sector industries.

topics.title: High technology industry and technopolies
topics.ncert_sections: Concept of High Technology Industry

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the features of high technology industry and its landscape.
Define technopolies and analyse why high-tech industries concentrate in planned areas.

topics.title: Nature of tertiary activities
topics.ncert_sections: Introduction

concepts.learning_objective: Explain that tertiary activities provide services for payment rather than producing tangible goods.
Distinguish tertiary activities from secondary activities on the basis of skills versus machinery.
Relate the share of workers in each sector to the stage of economic development.

topics.title: Trade and commerce
topics.ncert_sections: Trade and commerce; Retail Trading; Wholesale Trading

concepts.learning_objective: Describe rural and urban marketing centres and the services they offer.
Explain how periodic markets serve areas without regular markets.
Distinguish retail trading, non-store retailing and wholesale trading.

topics.title: Transport
topics.ncert_sections: Transport; Network and Accessibility; Factors Affecting Transport

concepts.learning_objective: Explain km distance, time distance and cost distance, and the use of isochrones.
Describe nodes, links and how the number of links shows accessibility.
Identify the factors that influence transport demand and route choice.

topics.title: Communication
topics.ncert_sections: Communication; Telecommunications

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the link between transport and communication and how it has changed.
Describe the role of telecommunications, mass media, satellites and the internet.

topics.title: Services and people engaged in tertiary activities
topics.ncert_sections: Services; People Engaged in Tertiary Activities

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish low-order and high-order services and physical and mental labour.
Describe regulated, professional, recreational and personal services and their location.
Interpret the share of service workers in developed and less developed countries.

topics.title: Tourism and medical tourism
topics.ncert_sections: Tourism; Tourist Regions; Tourist Attractions; Medical Services for Overseas Patients in India

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the meaning of tourism and its importance for jobs and other industries.
Identify climate, landscape, history and art, and culture and economy as tourist attractions.
Explain medical tourism and the outsourcing of medical tests and data interpretation.

topics.title: Quaternary and quinary activities
topics.ncert_sections: Quaternary Activities; The Quaternary Sector; Quinary Activities

concepts.learning_objective: Describe quaternary activities as knowledge-based services of information, research and development.
Explain quinary activities as the highly paid 'gold collar' work of top decision makers.

topics.title: Outsourcing, KPO and the digital divide
topics.ncert_sections: Outsourcing; The Digital Divide

concepts.learning_objective: Explain outsourcing and off-shoring and why work moves to countries such as India.
Distinguish knowledge processing outsourcing (KPO) from business process outsourcing (BPO).
Explain the digital divide between and within countries.

topics.title: Transport: meaning, network and modes
topics.ncert_sections: Transport; Modes of Transportation

concepts.learning_objective: Explain transport as an organised service and describe a transport network of nodes and links.
Distinguish the suitability of land, water, air and pipeline transport for different goods and distances.

topics.title: Land transport: pack animals, roads, highways and border roads
topics.ncert_sections: Land Transport; Roads; Highways; Border Roads

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the evolution of land transport and the merits and problems of road transport.
Identify major highways of the world and the purpose of border roads.

topics.title: Railways and trans-continental railways
topics.ncert_sections: Railways; Trans-Continental Railways

concepts.learning_objective: Describe railway gauges and the distribution of rail networks across continents.
Identify the routes and significance of the major trans-continental railways.

topics.title: Water transport: sea routes and shipping canals
topics.ncert_sections: Water Transport; Sea Routes; Coastal Shipping; Shipping Canals

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the major ocean trade routes and the factors that influence their traffic.
Compare the Suez and Panama Canals and explain their importance to world trade.

topics.title: Inland waterways
topics.ncert_sections: Inland Waterways

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the conditions for developing inland waterways and why some declined.
Identify the major inland waterways of the world and the regions they serve.

topics.title: Air transport and pipelines
topics.ncert_sections: Air Transport; Inter-Continental Air Routes; Pipelines

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the merits, limits and global distribution of air transport.
Explain the uses and examples of pipelines for transporting liquids and gases.

topics.title: Communications: telecommunication, satellites and cyberspace
topics.ncert_sections: Communications; Satellite Communication; Cyber Space - Internet

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the role of the telegraph, telephone and optic fibre cables in communication.
Explain how satellite communication changed the cost of communicating over distance.
Analyse the growth of the Internet and how cyberspace expands economic and social space.

topics.title: Trade, Barter, Money and the History of International Trade
topics.ncert_sections: Introduction; History of International Trade

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the barter system, its difficulties and how money and objects of intrinsic value replaced it.
Trace the major phases of international trade from the Silk Route to the post-war reduction of tariffs.

topics.title: Why International Trade Exists and Its Basis
topics.ncert_sections: Why Does International Trade Exist?; Basis of International Trade

concepts.learning_objective: State that international trade results from specialisation and rests on comparative advantage, complementarity and transferability.
Explain how resources, population, economic development, foreign investment and transport shape trade.

topics.title: Balance of Trade and Types of International Trade
topics.ncert_sections: Balance of Trade; Types of International Trade

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish favourable and unfavourable balance of trade and their implications for an economy.
Distinguish bilateral trade from multilateral trade and the grant of Most Favoured Nation status.

topics.title: Free Trade, Dumping and the World Trade Organisation
topics.ncert_sections: Case for Free Trade; Dumping; World Trade Organisation

concepts.learning_objective: Explain trade liberalisation and why dumped goods can harm domestic producers.
Describe the origin, functions and criticisms of the World Trade Organisation.

topics.title: Regional Trade Blocs and Concerns Related to International Trade
topics.ncert_sections: Regional Trade Blocs; Concerns Related to International Trade

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why regional trade blocs arose and their likely effect on trade between blocs.
Evaluate the benefits and harmful effects of international trade, including environmental concerns.

topics.title: Ports: Functions and Types by Cargo and Location
topics.ncert_sections: Gateways of International Trade: Ports; Types of Port (cargo handled, location)

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the facilities ports provide and how cargo handled reflects the development of the hinterland.
Classify ports as industrial, commercial or comprehensive, and as inland ports or out ports.

topics.title: Ports by Specialised Functions
topics.ncert_sections: Types of port on the basis of specialised functions

concepts.learning_objective: Identify ports of call and packet stations with their examples.
Identify oil, entrepot and naval ports and their examples.
